newsitem.title: USA: NY state bar backs muni "pay-to-play" ban.
newsitem.headline: NY state bar backs muni "pay-to-play" ban.

text.p: The New York State Bar Association's ethics panel on Tuesday said it generally backs the New York City bar's controversial ban on pay-to-play by bond lawyers.

"Our Committee agrees that the concerns raised by the practice of 'pay-to-play' should be addressed by restricting lawyers and law firms from seeking and receiving municipal bond work after making campaign contributions to or for the benefit of public officials who award such work," the state bar's committee on professional ethics announced.
The panel discussed the strategy in a two-page letter to Catherine Richard, president of the state bar association.
Pay-to-play refers to the practice of bond professionals giving contributions to elected municipal officials in return for bond business.

The Association of the Bar of the City of New York last year proposed a rule that would bar muni lawyers that solicit or make contributions to municipal clients from engaging in bond business for two years with those government.

New York City's bar on March 10 urged the state's Administrative Board, which sets standards for thousands of New York lawyers, to adopt the rule statewide. The city bar also wants the American Bar Association to endorse the plan at its annual meeting this summer.

"The practice of many municipal bond lawyers making substantial campaign contributions followed by the receipt of government business raises serious concerns (involving) government integrity and legal ethics," the New York State bar panel's letter says.
The panel said it endorses the City bar's recommendation "in general" but has no position on the particular proposal.

"Many important issues merit further consideration," the panel said, including whether pay-to-play should be restricted by court rule or legislation, whether law firm members who do not engage in muni bond work should be covered, and if the rule should extend to spouses.
